request.question: What if nobody can replace the Pilbara Electric Motors loader motor?

answer:
**If nobody can replace the Pilbara Electric Motors loader motor, the operation faces a stockout starting 1 March 2027 and stands to lose 1.81 Mt of ore production over 36 days, putting USD 196.0 million of revenue at risk and affecting approximately 10 cargoes.**

The M1 motor plant fire (alert ALR-2026-1022-02, 22 October 2026) closes the sole supplier of the ship loader drive motor 200 kW (MZ-SP-A101) for 180 days. Current inventory provides 144 days of cover. With no alternate supplier identified—single-source status triggers a **Review** under the sourcing policy—the 36-day gap cannot be closed. One dependent fleet asset (the ship loader) would halt, blocking 50,288 t/day ore throughput valued at USD 5.4 million/day.

| Scenario | Gap (days) | Ore at risk (t) | Revenue at risk (USD) | Cargoes at risk | Source |
|----------|------------|-----------------|----------------------|-----------------|---------|
| No action | 36 | 1,810,368 | 196,049,772 | 10.0 | Stand-in, SAP BDC, Operations (MIXED) |
| Best alternate | 36 | 1,810,368 | 196,049,772 | 10.0 | Stand-in, SAP BDC, Operations (MIXED) |

**Chain:** Fire → 180-day plant closure → stockout 15 March 2027 → ship loader down → 50 kt/day ore throughput lost → ~10 cargoes missed → USD 196 M revenue loss.

**Recommended next step:** Immediately engage engineering and procurement to either (a) qualify an emergency alternate motor supplier with expedited audit, or (b) explore refurbishment of any retired motor stock or cross-site transfer to bridge the 36-day shortfall.
